title: Feature — Make WCode the Windows application test lifecycle authority
description: Vaporize assigns Windows application build, install, and run lifecycle to WCode but rejects application testing. Visual and UI-test packages therefore rebuild private staging and launch infrastructure instead of composing the engineering-owned lifecycle service.
acceptanceCriteria: `vaporize test wcode --artifact app` is a supported canonical operation.

The operation builds the selected SwiftPM application product, materializes its runtime artifacts and project.pkl resources, launches the exact staged executable, and exposes its process and installation identity to a caller-supplied test journey.
Run and test share one WCode materialization and launch contract rather than maintaining independent executable-location logic.
The test lifecycle can retain a launched application for interactive inspection or terminate it deterministically after an automated journey.
Typed lifecycle and test receipts distinguish build, materialization, launch, assertion, screenshot, and teardown outcomes.
SwiftUUI Museum Windows visual tests pass through the new lifecycle without owning SwiftPM build, runtime-bundle copying, or raw process launch.
implementationInstructions: Extend the existing WCode application authority; do not create a second Windows app runner.
Promote build, materialization, executable location, environment projection, launch, and teardown into reusable Vaporize/WCode services callable by both `run` and `test`.
Keep UI automation and domain assertions in the consuming test package; Vaporize owns lifecycle orchestration and typed process evidence.
Support caller-declared runtime artifacts and the canonical project.pkl resource projection.
Add CUJ coverage for successful launch, retained interactive launch, assertion failure, application crash, missing runtime artifact, and deterministic teardown.
Use CommonProcess and existing Vaporize issue reporting; do not introduce raw Process or print-based diagnostics.
Preserve existing `vaporize run wcode --artifact app` behavior while routing it through the shared lifecycle service.
blockers: The real SwiftUUI Museum dispatch reaches Vaporize's shared i18n source gate and is blocked by its existing missing-passport and loose-copy findings. Capturing an International Law baseline or provisioning approved copy requires an explicit product-governance disposition.
notes: The 2026-08-28 source review found the explicit guard `WCode has no application test lifecycle contract.` The first implementation slice now supports an explicit executable driver, launches the app through CommonProcess retained lifecycle, exports reserved live-process identity, tears down on driver success or failure, and emits combined lifecycle evidence. Parser/routing tests and the retained-process tests pass. SwiftUUI Museum no longer needs to own build or launch in its driver, but the full real-app receipt remains blocked at the shared i18n source gate; retained interactive inspection and richer failure CUJs also remain open.
